## 2. The host-free reference has an exact nuisance polynomial

For analysis only, use the reference with H_G spin independent and no
longitudinal host force/bias, retaining the SAME finite pointer dynamics.
This is not a supplied physical switch. Delta remains on during the tags.
At Delta=0 a tag's odd-weighted instrument has diagonal weights(+m,-m)
and zero offdiagonal weight: the Gaussian product kernel is real/even and
the response is odd. Thus its weighted map is exactly

    J_F(rho)=m{sigma_z,rho}/2.                           (2)

For two vertices BOTH in the free gap, the zero-transverse finite tags
therefore give M cos(Delta T). Their contribution to c_2(T) is -M T^2/2,
for any initial spin state. Two tag-internal vertices give a gap-independent
coefficient; one vertex in the free gap and one inside a tag gives a term
linear in T. The unperturbed reference has no other T dependence. Hence

    c_2,ref(T)=-M T^2/2+A T+B.                          (3)

The unknown A,B include all finite-tag shape/backaction effects and are
common across the three geometries. This ordered-word decomposition is the
central claim to reconstruct independently; it does not drop the actual
transverse evolution during a tag.

With v=(-1,2,-1), equations(3) give

    sum_r v_r M=0,
    sum_r v_r c_2,ref(T_r)=M h^2.                       (4)

Thus the curvature contrast preserves the bare Delta^2 signal while killing
both unknown tag nuisance coefficients, as well as the unknown zero baseline.

## 3. A deliberately conservative host comparison

Let B_host bound the unconditional state L2 norm of the longitudinal
frequency (2lambda Y_G(u)+epsilon)/hbar in the HOST-FREE reference applied
to the actual old state, averaged over its earlier records. H_G evolves
that host independently of all spin/pointer operations. Reference sigma_x
insertions and finite tags therefore leave this host marginal unchanged.
The actual linear-host source formula with the entire old bounded-force/
mechanical-meter history retained supplies the Y_G bound; it is not a
conditional Gaussian or conditional-energy assertion. The host force after
the trial start is removed only in this mathematical comparison. Direct
meter bias is retained exactly in both references and is NOT part of B_host.

## 2. The actual finite-band host supplies the comparison norm

The actual input need not be Gaussian locally. At every predeclared trial
cut it has the source-generated history of the accepted calibration work.
Its FREE host evolution after that cut obeys

    Y_free(t)=Y_in(t)+int_(s<0) chi_ret(t-s)
                                [lambda sigma_old(s)+F_old(s)]ds,
    ||Y_free(t)||_2<=Y_max=sqrt(V_in)+lambda_max Lambda+Y_oldsource,
    Lambda=int_0^infty |chi_ret|<infty.                   (1)

The norm is UNCONDITIONAL over old records. The Gaussian incoming marginal,
all retained old mechanical sources, and absence of an uncounted free
bound mode are the existing actual input contract. No conditional bath
energy, new local thermal state or nonlinear equilibration is assumed.

In the HOST-FREE current reference every meter, Gaussian pointer momentum
and inserted sigma_x acts only on spin/pointers. They commute with H_G.
Hence they do not change the free host's reduced state or the bound(1),
even when the old spin and host were entangled. This proves the required
all-inserted-path moment bound directly, rather than postulating one:

    B_host=(2lambda_max Y_max+epsilon_max)/hbar.           (2)

There is NO current gP term in(2); the actual finite tags are retained on
both sides of the comparison. An insertion is a local spin unitary and
adds no mechanical impulse. Old direct Y forces remain in Y_oldsource.

For any fixed order2 ket or bra word, telescope host-full and host-free
propagators. State-induced Duhamel along the host-free path gives vector
norm error at most B_host tau/2. Averaging conditional old states uses
HS Minkowski and(1), not a uniform conditional bound. A bounded readout
product O of norm at most R=R_1R_2 therefore changes its matrix element
by at most R B_host tau. The total order2 ket/bra integration weight is
tau^2/2. Consequently

    E_past |c_2,actual-c_2,ref|<=R B_host tau^3/2.         (3)

All higher transverse terms have the ordinary bounded remainder
R[exp(|Delta|tau)-1-|Delta|tau-Delta^2 tau^2/2]. Combined with the exact
baseline and first cancellation, this proves the root draft's relative
signal-error constant at its ACTUAL finite-band/source-history scope.
The host-free reference is only a proof comparison, not an experimental
coupling switch or a newly prepared state.
